newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian lower house approves 1997 austerity budget.
newsitem.headline: Italian lower house approves 1997 austerity budget.

text.p: Italy's lower house of parliament approved the centre-left government's 1997 austerity budget on Saturday, a parliamentary official said.
The package, designed to cut a massive 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's projected state deficit, now passes to the upper house (Senate), which has until Christmas to approve the bill.

The draft law, which Prime Minister Romano Prodi says is vital if Italy is to become a founder member of the planned single European currency, is hotly contested by opposition parties. They boycotted the final vote. The package was approved by 314 votes and none against.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said earlier this month that Italy would seek to put the lira back into the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) once the budget had passed through the turbulent lower house.

However in an interview with La Stampa newspaper on Saturday he dampened hopes of an immediate return. "We (still) have to evaluate if...we will have to wait for ratification in both houses," he was quoted as saying.
